messages.author: ddc91303cb21ac62
messages.subject: Custom labels - Facet Plot
parts:
Hello there,

I am a little confused as to how to make custom labels when making a
faceted plot. Perhaps I am just using poor search terms but I can't
seem to find the answer to this. I've made up a trivial example below.
How can I change, for example, the A's into and expression like this:
expression(delta^15~N).

Thanks in advance!

Sam


library(ggplot2)
x <-runif(9, 0, 125)
data <- as.data.frame(x)
data$y <--runif(9, 0, 125)
data$z <- factor(c("A","A","A","B","B","B","C","C","C"))
data$yy <- factor(c("a","b","c"))

pg <- ggplot(data, aes(x, y)) + geom_point(shape = 2) + facet_grid(z ~
yy, scales="free")
pg

messages.subject: Re: Custom labels - Facet Plot
parts:
Sam,
I haven't quite figured it out myself but this seems to work.

From: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/2403466/greek-letters-in-ggplot-strip-text

#####
###make a labeller
label_parseall <- function(variable, value) {
plyr::llply(value, function(x) parse(text = paste(x)))
}

#change factors into what you want parsed/expressions

library(ggplot2)
x <-runif(9, 0, 125)
data <- as.data.frame(x)
data$y <--runif(9, 0, 125)
data$z <- factor(c("delta^15~N","delta^15~N","delta^15~N","B","B","B","C","C","C"))
data$yy <- factor(c("a","b","c"))
pg <- ggplot(data, aes(x, y)) + geom_point(shape = 2) + facet_grid(z ~

yy, scales="free", labeller= label_parseall)
pg

###Profit?

Brandon

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Custom labels - Facet Plot
parts: Hi:

"So for example
instead of a plot with A, B and C as the facet labels, I would like to
manually be able to change it to Alan, Blair and Chris. This is done
with the strip and strip.custom commands in lattice. So is there an
easier way to re-label the facets in ggplot2?"

There is an 'obvious' way - make them the levels of your factor in the data frame before you invoke ggplot(), or
alternatively, make a parallel factor with those names as levels and use it as a faceting variable. It's more work to change the labels inside the ggplot, and it's unnecessary.

Using your example,

data$lab <- factor(rep(c('Alan', 'Blair', 'Chris'), each = 3))
pg <- ggplot(data, aes(x, y)) + geom_point(shape = 2)

pg + facet_grid(lab ~ yy, scales = 'free')


HTH,
Dennis

messages.subject: Re: Custom labels - Facet Plot
parts: Hi:

"I just recently made the switch from lattice and this is
quite simple thing to do in lattice. So I was looking for something
similar in ggplot. But I see that really the best solution is the
parallel factor option."

Different paradigms, different solutions :)  You could save yourself some time (and code) in lattice by using the same principle, though, since you have to use the strip argument to specify changes in the strip labels. The point is that if you can pre-arrange (or design) the data to simplify the plot calls in either lattice or ggplot2, you can save yourself a lot of work.

Dennis
